title: Revise firstmate study page: define terms, fix diagram, add titles
summary: Revise the generated firstmate explainer page, whose text lives in studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json and is rendered by xtask/src/site.rs. The goal is a newcomer-readable page: terms defined at first use, one word per concept, no unexplained jargon, and the t10 diagram consistent with t4. The opening and Next steps stay as they are.

defaults_applied.how: The change is in Rust (xtask site renderer) and JSON data; no other language added.
site.rs tests updated for titles and labels; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The criteria check the rendered page text and a successful site build, not only that fields exist.
The verifier runs the site build and tests.
One focused change to the page's text and renderer.
New wording is written for a newcomer reader.
Every new sentence cites existing claims.
Recovered the page source from the repository instead of asking.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: a first-time reader (the rating audience) can follow the page; the page at doodla.github.io/athena is generated by `cargo run -p xtask -- site` from the study JSON and xtask/src/site.rs, so edits go there, not to HTML.
Rationale records deny unknown fields, so the ra1–ra6 titles are stored in intro.json (a new key read by site.rs) rather than adding a field to rationales.json and the schema.
Item 4 is resolved by explanation rather than changing model.json, since a yolo merge keeps the task Ready until teardown; if the producer prefers to fix the diagram, model.json may change.
The new term for the deciding agent is 'firstmate's agent' (or 'mate') and 'worker' stays for task agents; 'decided by agent' then means firstmate's agent.
Show-time labels like 'agent'/'code' are mapped in site.rs so model.json values and study validation stay valid.
Study files are pinned data; no claims or sources change, only intro text and rendering.

acceptance_criteria.text: In 'Start here', the first use of 'captain' and of 'yolo' carries an inline definition (captain: the person who approves merges; yolo: the setting under which firstmate merges green work itself). The Start here wording appears before any use of either term.

The glossary has a 'home' entry (a firstmate home: the directory/instance with its own backlog and tasks, which a secondmate persists in), cited to existing claims, and the 'backlog item' and 'secondmate' entries use the term consistently with it.

Two different terms are used throughout: one for firstmate's deciding agent (e.g. 'firstmate's agent') and one for worker agents ('worker'). The deciders list, the glossary and every 'decided by' / 'checked by' label on the transition cards say which one is meant, and the word 'agent' no longer means both.

The t10 card is consistent with t4: either the page explains in t10's summary or the transitions lead-in why a yolo merge keeps the task in Ready (the merge is a step that is followed by t4's teardown, which moves it to Done), or t10 is changed so the diagram does not contradict t4's trigger 'the merge lands'. No claim is left uncited.

Each design-choice card ra1–ra6 shows a short topic title (for example, backlog change paired with the record change; deferral at capacity; no concurrency cap; fail-fast project lock; reopen on open captain call; place freed at recorded PR) next to its id. Titles come from the study data, not hard-coded in a way that skips the claim-citation rules.

The 'reopened' state no longer shows the bare tag 'terminal-success' (or the tag is explained in the States lead-in as 'final: the task has ended, with the item left open for the captain'), and the label shown for 'done' and 'reopened' matches the glossary's wording.
The lede either explains the study identifier (what it names and that it is a label for this study run) or no longer shows it; the pinned commit line is unchanged.
The opening paragraphs (title, Athena and study ledes) and the Next steps section are unchanged apart from the lede identifier fix in (7).

Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` from the repository root; all pass, including the xtask site tests. Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`; it succeeds with no missing-claim or uncited-element error, so the generated page builds from the revised data.

out_of_scope: Changing the opening ledes about Athena and the study, apart from the study identifier
Re-studying firstmate or changing claims.json, pin.json or sources
Changing the study schema or validation rules
Redesigning the page layout or styling
departures: Seven distinct edits across data and renderer, with a wording-judgment verifier, make a pass slightly less likely than the reference; cost is a little higher.
